rationale: No exact solution exists in this template. Even nearest-colour keys cannot distinguish demonstration 1 row 4 columns 0 and 1: both see only colour 1 to the right, but only column 1 becomes 7. The other key kinds also merge pixels requiring different outputs.

Pixel count distinguishes the demonstrated large objects and maps the small objects to 0, reproducing all demonstrations and the counterexample. Generalisation beyond demonstrated counts is limited because unseen counts remain unchanged.

No exact solution exists in this template. Object recolouring cannot move the interior colours onto previously empty exterior corners. Choosing a different background still cannot recolour individual cells within a zero component differently.

No exact solution exists in this template. Demonstration 2 row 3 columns 2 and 6 have identical own colours and identical neighbourhoods, yet column 2 becomes 8 and column 6 stays 0. Every supported key therefore has conflicting required outputs.

No exact solution exists in this template. Demonstration 3 row 1 columns 3 and 5 have identical complete neighbourhoods, but column 3 stays 8 and column 5 becomes 9. None of the supported neighbourhood keys can distinguish them.

No exact solution exists in this template. Source-colour painting cannot introduce colour 2 at crossings when no source has colour 2. Constant painting with colour 2 would also replace the required source-coloured rays.
